newsitem.title: HONG KONG: OOIL seeks OK for connected transactions.
newsitem.headline: OOIL seeks OK for connected transactions.

text.p: Shipping giant Orient Overseas (International) Ltd (OOIL) said on Tuesday it was seeking shareholders' endorsement of commercial transactions connected to companies controlled by the brother-in-law of its chairman, C.H. Tung.
Tung has long been tipped as a frontrunner to become leader of Hong Kong's government after the 1997 handover to China.

The company said on Tuesday it had made provisional orders to buy containers from Associated Industries (Shanghai) Inc (AIS) and proposed to make a further provisional order for containers from Associated Industries China Inc (AIC).
Both AIS and AIC are controlled by John Peng, Tung's brother-in-law.

The group has been buying containers from AIC, AIS and their affiliates since 1979, but it did not occur to management that such ongoing purchases could constitute connected transactions requiring the issue of a press notice each time such purchase was entered into and the disclosure of details of such purchases in annual reports, OOIL said.

The latest purchases were estimated at US$13.2 million or 2.17 percent of the consolidated net tangible assets of OOIL, and the company said they would be made at armslength on commerical terms in the ordinary course of its business.
The money for the purchases in the past nine years ranged between US$2.1 million and US$11.6 million, it said.
OOIL also said two of its units entered into an agency agreement with Chinese Maritime Transport Ltd (CMT), another company controlled by Peng, 25 years ago.

They also have a management contract with CMT in 1986 under which CMT was appointed general manager of certain container terminal facilities in Taiwan and to act as the non-exclusive research and development agent of such subsidiaries, it said.
The management contract would continue until 1999.
OOIL said it ould seek shareholder approval to grant the mandate to the directors of the companies to authorise the group to enter into such transactions in a special general meeting.
